question: A search head has successfully joined a single site indexer cluster. Which command is used to configure the same search head to join another indexer cluster?
explanation:
You can configure a search head to search across multiple indexer clusters. Configure the search head for one of the clusters in the usual way and then proceed with adding another cluster.
For example, to add the search head to a cluster whose manager node is located at https://10.160.31.200:8089, run this command:
splunk add cluster-manager https://10.160.31.200:8089 -secret your_key
PS - The term "manager node" replaces the term "master node"

question: Of the following types of files within an index bucket, which file type may consume the most disk?
explanation: The correct answer is inverted index (.tsidx). This allows fast full text searches and required for searchable buckets. Typically, the rawdata file is 15% the size of the pre-indexed data, and the TSIDX files are approximately 35% of the size of the pre-indexed data. When you combine the two file sizes, the rawdata and TSIDX represent approximately 50% of pre-indexed data volume.

question: Which of the following is a valid use case that a search head cluster addresses?
choices: A. Provide redundancy in the event a search peer fails.
explanation:
Search Head Clustering in Splunk addresses the following key requirements:
High Availability (HA): Ensures that users can access the search functionality even if one or more search heads fail.
Load Balancing: Distributes search and user activity across multiple search head cluster members, improving performance and preventing overload on a single search head.
Consistency of Knowledge Objects: Provides seamless replication and synchronization of knowledge objects (e.g., saved searches, dashboards, alerts) across all cluster members, ensuring a consistent user experience regardless of which search head is accessed.
Scalability: Allows organizations to add more search heads to handle an increasing number of users or search workloads.

question: Which index-time props.conf attributes impact indexing performance? (select all that apply)
explanation: SHOULD_LINEMERGE and LINE_BREAKER are index-time (parsing) settings that control how the incoming stream is broken into events, so they directly affect indexing performance - SHOULD_LINEMERGE in particular invokes the more costly line-merging logic. REPORT is a search-time field-extraction directive and does not affect indexing throughput. ANNOTATE_PUNCT only controls creation of the punct field and has negligible performance impact by comparison.

question: When determining where a Splunk forwarder is trying to send data, which of the following searches can provide assistance?
choices: A. index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd metrics destHost | dedup destHost
B. index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd metrics inputHost | dedup inputHost
C. index=_internal sourcetype=internal metrics destHost | dedup destHost
D. index=_metrics sourcetype=splunkd metrics destHost | dedup destHost
explanation: To identify the destination indexers a Splunk forwarder is attempting to send data to, execute the search: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd metrics destHost | dedup destHost. This query leverages the internal Splunk logs (index=_internal), specifically the metrics log events generated by forwarders, and focuses on the destHost field, which captures the destination hosts (typically indexers). The dedup command ensures that only unique entries for each destination host are displayed, providing a concise list of all indexers the forwarder is currently communicating with or attempting to reach.

question: In a distributed environment, knowledge object bundles are replicated from the search head to which location on the search peer(s)?
explanation:
As part of the distributed search process, the search head periodically distributes its knowledge bundle to its search peers. This process is known as knowledge bundle replication.
Location of the knowledge bundle
On the search head, the knowledge bundles resides under the $SPLUNK_HOME/var/run directory. The bundles have the extension .bundle for full bundles or .delta for delta bundles. They are tar files, so you can run tar tvf against them to see the contents.
During replication, the knowledge bundle gets distributed to the SPLUNK_HOME/var/run/searchpeers directory on each search peer. Because the knowledge bundle reside in a different location on the search peers than on the search head, search scripts must not hardcode paths to resources.

question: Which of the following options can improve reliability of syslog delivery to Splunk? (Select all that apply.)
choices: B. Use a network load balancer to direct syslog traffic to active backend syslog listeners.
C. Configure UDP inputs on each Splunk indexer to receive data directly.
D. Use one or more syslog servers to persist data with a Universal Forwarder to send the data to Splunk indexers.
explanation:
TCP: Offers a reliable connection-oriented service, ensuring that messages are received in order and without loss. While TCP reduces the risk of lost messages, it introduces more overhead and complexity due to connection management.
UDP: Traditionally, syslog used UDP for its simplicity and low overhead. UDP does not guarantee delivery, making it faster but less reliable. In high-volume environments, this can lead to lost messages. UDP may be more commonly used in the same subnet solutions.
Here is the widely used solution by customers -
Rsyslog or Syslog NG combined with Universal forwarder (UF)/heavy forwarder (HF): Use a Splunk UF or HF to monitor and ingest files written out by a syslog server, such as rsyslog or syslog-ng. This solution is widely used by customers with existing syslog infrastructure.

question: The KV store forms its own cluster within a SHC. What is the maximum number of SHC members KV store will form?
explanation: The KV store forms its own cluster within a SHC. The maximum number of SHC members KV store will form is 50. The KV store cluster is a subset of the SHC members that are responsible for replicating and storing the KV store data. The KV store cluster can have up to 50 members, but only 20 of them can be active at any given time. The other members are standby members that can take over if an active member fails. The KV store cluster cannot have more than 50 members, nor can it have an unlimited number of members. The KV store cluster cannot have 25 or 100 members, because these numbers are not multiples of 5, which is the minimum replication factor for the KV store cluster

question: Which of the following statements describe converting a non-clustered indexer to a cluster peer node? (select all that apply)
choices: A. Apps must be deleted from $SPLUNK_HOME/ etc/master-apps.
B. Apps must be re-distributed via $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/master-apps.
C. Existing buckets are not replicated.
D. Only new data coming into this peer is replicated.
explanation: You can begin eliminating incorrect options here. Option 3 mentions deleting apps from the $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/master-apps directory, which is unnecessary when adding a new peer to an indexer cluster. All apps deployed through the cluster manager (formerly cluster master) are automatically placed in the $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/peer-apps directory on the indexer peers. Similarly, Option 4 incorrectly states that only new data received by the newly added peer will be replicated. In reality, data received by all peers in the cluster is subject to replication, ensuring high availability and redundancy across the entire cluster.

question: When implementing KV Store Collections in a search head cluster, which of the following considerations is true?
choices: A. The KV Store Primary coordinates with the search head cluster captain when collection content changes.
B. The KV Store Collection will not allow for changes to content if there are more than 50 search heads in the cluster.
C. The search head cluster captain is also the KV Store Primary when collection content changes.
D. Each search head in the cluster independently updates its KV store collection when collection content changes.
explanation: In a search head cluster the KV Store forms its own cluster with a KV Store primary, a role separate from the SHC captain. When collection content changes, the KV Store primary coordinates with the search head cluster captain so the update replicates consistently to all members. The KV Store primary and SHC captain are not necessarily the same node (ruling out C), members do not each update independently (ruling out D), and the 50-member limit applies to KV Store cluster size, not to whether content changes are permitted.
